meta.name: AI Glossary for the AI Term Explainer Agent
meta.note: Term list taken from the source page. Explanations, mental models and quizzes are original wording written for the agent, not copies of the source text.

schema.id: slug used as the primary key
schema.aliases: other names or abbreviations, useful for lookup
schema.quiz: one multiple-choice question: q, options[4], answer_index, explanation
schema.review_status: draft | approved | rejected (human-in-the-loop gate before the agent serves it)
schema.source_truncated: true when the source page text was cut off and wording is partly inferred

terms.simple: An attack where someone quietly interferes with the process of training or distilling a model so the result is compromised.
terms.mental_model: A student studies from a tutor's notes while someone secretly swaps in a few wrong pages.

quiz.q: What is the attacker's aim in an adversarial distillation attack?
options: Quietly interfere with the training process
quiz.explanation: The attack targets the training/distillation process itself, so the resulting model is compromised.

terms.simple: A hypothetical AI that can learn and reason across almost any task at human level or better.
terms.mental_model: One assistant that can file your taxes, debug code and plan a trip, without being rebuilt for each job.

quiz.q: What most distinguishes AGI from today's narrow AI?
options: It works across a wide range of tasks
quiz.explanation: AGI means broad, general ability rather than skill in a single task.

terms.simple: AI that pursues a goal by planning steps, using tools and adjusting based on feedback.
terms.mental_model: You say 'book me a flight under $400' and it searches, compares, and fills the booking form itself.

options: Only answering one question at a time
Planning and taking multi-step actions with tools
quiz.explanation: Agentic systems plan, act through tools, and adapt to results.

terms.simple: Making sure an AI's goals and behavior match what people actually intend and value.
terms.mental_model: You ask a robot vacuum to 'clean the floor' and it doesn't throw out your keys to get the floor clearer.

options: Matching AI behavior to human intent
quiz.explanation: Alignment keeps AI behavior consistent with human values and instructions.

terms.simple: Standard tests used to compare how well different AI systems perform a task.
terms.mental_model: Like a common exam every student sits so you can compare scores fairly.

options: They allow fair comparison across models
quiz.explanation: A shared test lets you compare systems on equal terms.

terms.simple: The skill of working with AI effectively and responsibly, knowing what it can and cannot do.
terms.mental_model: Knowing when to trust a GPS and when to notice it's sending you into a lake.

quiz.q: Which is part of AI fluency?
quiz.explanation: Fluency includes checking outputs and understanding limitations.

terms.simple: The field focused on making AI behave reliably and avoid causing harm, even in unexpected situations.
terms.mental_model: Crash testing and seatbelts, but for AI systems.

quiz.explanation: It aims to keep AI reliable and non-harmful at scale.

terms.simple: The layers of hardware, software and compute that together support building and running AI.
terms.mental_model: Like a restaurant: farms, kitchen, chefs and waiters all stacked to deliver one meal.

quiz.explanation: It is the full set of layers supporting the AI lifecycle.

terms.simple: The end-to-end sequence of building an AI system: data prep, training, testing and deployment.
terms.mental_model: An assembly line where each station hands a better product to the next.

quiz.explanation: Data comes first, then training and testing, then deployment.

terms.simple: A step-by-step set of instructions for solving a problem.
terms.mental_model: A cooking recipe: follow the steps and you get the dish.

quiz.q: An algorithm is best described as:
quiz.explanation: It is an ordered set of steps to reach a result.

terms.simple: When many organizations use the same or very similar AI systems or data, so they all make the same mistakes.
terms.mental_model: Every bank using the same credit model, so one flaw rejects the same people everywhere.

quiz.q: What is the main risk of algorithmic monoculture?
options: Shared errors affecting everyone at once
quiz.explanation: Uniform systems fail in uniform ways, so errors spread widely.

terms.simple: A network of AI systems that share information and coordinate their actions like one collective.
terms.mental_model: A swarm of delivery drones that share traffic info so all of them reroute at once.

options: AI agents that share info and coordinate
quiz.explanation: It describes AI systems acting together through shared information.

terms.simple: The science of making machines do things that normally need human intelligence.
terms.mental_model: Your phone unlocking by recognizing your face.

quiz.q: Who coined the term 'artificial intelligence' in 1955?
quiz.explanation: John McCarthy introduced the term in 1955.

terms.simple: A way for a model to focus on the most relevant parts of its input when producing output.
terms.mental_model: Highlighting the key sentence in a paragraph before answering a question about it.

quiz.q: What does attention let a model do?
options: Focus on the most relevant parts
quiz.explanation: It weights input parts by relevance.

terms.simple: Technology doing a task exactly the way a human defined it.
terms.mental_model: An email rule that moves every invoice into a folder.

quiz.q: In automation, who defines what to do?
quiz.explanation: Automation follows predefined human instructions, unlike agentic AI that plans for itself.

terms.simple: How a neural network learns from errors by tracing blame backward through its layers.
terms.mental_model: A team reviews a failed project from the end and finds which step caused the miss.

options: Sending error backward to adjust weights
quiz.explanation: Error signals travel backward to update the weights.

terms.simple: Graphs that show how variables influence each other using probabilities.
terms.mental_model: A map showing that rain raises the chance of wet roads, which raises the chance of accidents.

quiz.explanation: They model dependencies between variables with probabilities.

terms.simple: When an AI system's results unfairly favor or disadvantage certain groups.
terms.mental_model: A hiring tool trained on past hires keeps preferring the same type of candidate.

quiz.q: A common source of AI bias is:
quiz.explanation: Models often inherit patterns and imbalances from their training data.

terms.simple: Datasets so large that ordinary tools can't process them, often analyzed with AI to find patterns.
terms.mental_model: Millions of card swipes scanned at once to spot fraud.

quiz.q: Big data is mainly defined by:
options: Being too large for traditional tools
quiz.explanation: Its volume exceeds what conventional software handles.

terms.simple: A program that holds a conversation with people by text or voice.
terms.mental_model: The support window on a shopping site that answers 'where's my order?'

quiz.explanation: Chatbots interact with people in conversation.

terms.simple: Software whose code is kept private and can't be viewed or modified by the public.
terms.mental_model: A sealed appliance: you can use it but can't open it up.

quiz.explanation: The owner restricts access to the underlying code.

terms.simple: AI that lets computers understand images and video.
terms.mental_model: A phone camera that outlines faces before you take the photo.

options: Visual data like images and video
quiz.explanation: It interprets visual information.

terms.simple: The amount of text a model can take in and consider at once.
terms.mental_model: A desk: only the papers that fit on it are in front of you.

quiz.q: What happens to text beyond the context window?
options: The model can't see it in that request
quiz.explanation: Only content within the window is available to the model.

terms.simple: Learning by comparing similar and different examples to see what sets them apart.
terms.mental_model: Learning to tell cats from dogs by seeing pairs side by side.

quiz.explanation: It pulls similar items together and pushes different ones apart.

terms.simple: Creating extra training examples by modifying data you already have.
terms.mental_model: Flipping and cropping photos so one picture becomes ten.

quiz.explanation: It generates variations without new collection.

terms.simple: Digging through large datasets to find hidden patterns and trends.
terms.mental_model: A store finding that people who buy diapers often buy snacks too.

quiz.explanation: It uncovers patterns using statistics and ML.

terms.simple: An attack that plants bad or mislabeled data in a model's training set to corrupt it.
terms.mental_model: Someone slips wrong answers into a student's textbook before the exam.

quiz.explanation: Attackers tamper with training data to affect model behavior.

terms.simple: A model that makes predictions by asking a chain of yes/no questions.
terms.mental_model: A 20-questions game that narrows down to an answer.

quiz.explanation: It splits data on features step by step.

terms.simple: Machine learning with many-layered neural networks that learn complex patterns on their own.
terms.mental_model: Your photo app learning to recognize your dog from thousands of pictures.

quiz.explanation: Deep means networks with many layers.

terms.simple: Generative models that create content by learning to remove noise step by step.
terms.mental_model: A sculptor revealing an image from a block of static.

quiz.explanation: They learn to denoise random noise into new content.

terms.simple: Cutting down the number of variables in data while keeping the important information.
terms.mental_model: Summarizing a 50-question survey into three key scores.

options: Simplify data while keeping key info
quiz.explanation: It compresses features with minimal loss of meaning.

terms.simple: Lists of numbers that capture the meaning of words, images or other items.
terms.mental_model: GPS coordinates for meaning: 'king' and 'queen' land near each other.

quiz.explanation: They encode meaning as numerical vectors.

terms.simple: Combining several models so the group predicts better than any one alone.
terms.mental_model: Asking a panel of doctors instead of one.

options: Combined models are often more accurate
quiz.explanation: Pooling models reduces individual errors.

terms.simple: Building and using AI in line with human values, fairness, transparency and societal well-being.
terms.mental_model: A loan model that is tested to make sure it treats applicants fairly.

quiz.explanation: It aligns AI design and use with human values.

terms.simple: Older AI that imitates a human expert using stored facts and if-then rules.
terms.mental_model: A checklist program that diagnoses car trouble from rules a mechanic wrote.

options: If-then rules and a knowledge base
quiz.explanation: They reason with hand-built rules and facts.

terms.simple: Methods that make an AI's decisions understandable instead of a black box.
terms.mental_model: A loan denial that tells you 'income too low and debt too high.'

quiz.explanation: It makes AI decisions interpretable to humans.

terms.simple: Training a shared model across many devices without moving their private data.
terms.mental_model: Your phone's keyboard improves from your typing without sending your messages to a server.

quiz.q: In federated learning, the raw data:
quiz.explanation: Only model updates are shared, not the raw data.

terms.simple: Learning a new task from just a handful of examples.
terms.mental_model: Showing a chatbot three sample emails and it writes the fourth in the same style.

quiz.explanation: It generalizes from very few examples.

terms.simple: Taking a pre-trained model and training it more on specific data for a specific job.
terms.mental_model: A general doctor doing a residency to become a heart specialist.

quiz.explanation: It adapts an existing model with additional training.

terms.simple: Large models trained on broad data that can be adapted to many different tasks.
terms.mental_model: A strong base layer of a building that many different apps are built on.

quiz.explanation: It serves as a base for many downstream uses.

terms.simple: A top-tier general-purpose AI model at or near the cutting edge.
terms.mental_model: The newest flagship phone versus last year's model.

options: Among the most capable current models
quiz.explanation: Frontier means at the leading edge of capability.

terms.simple: AI that creates new content such as text, images, music, code or video.
terms.mental_model: Typing 'a cat in a spacesuit' and getting a brand-new picture.

quiz.explanation: It produces new text, images, audio, and more.

terms.simple: Two networks compete, one making fakes and one spotting them, until the fakes look real.
terms.mental_model: A counterfeiter and a detective who each get better by outsmarting the other.

quiz.q: The two parts of a GAN are:
quiz.explanation: The generator creates, the discriminator judges.

terms.simple: A family of language models built on the transformer that generate human-like text from prompts.
terms.mental_model: An autocomplete that can write a whole essay.

quiz.q: GPT is built on which architecture?
quiz.explanation: The T in GPT stands for Transformer.

terms.simple: A chip that does many calculations in parallel, which is ideal for training AI.
terms.mental_model: A thousand calculators working together instead of one fast one.

quiz.q: Why are GPUs good for AI?
quiz.explanation: AI training involves huge parallel computations.

terms.simple: When an AI states false or made-up information as if it were fact.
terms.mental_model: A chatbot confidently citing a book that doesn't exist.

options: A confident but false AI output
quiz.explanation: The model produces plausible-sounding but incorrect content.

terms.simple: Designing AI around human needs, values and well-being.
terms.mental_model: A medical AI built with doctors and patients, not just engineers.

quiz.explanation: Human well-being guides design and deployment.

terms.simple: The study of how people use and interact with computers.
terms.mental_model: Why swipe-to-refresh feels natural on a phone.

quiz.explanation: It focuses on the human side of using computer systems.

terms.simple: Keeping a person involved to review, correct or approve an AI's work.
terms.mental_model: An AI drafts a refund email and a manager approves it before sending.

quiz.explanation: A person provides feedback or approval within the process.

terms.simple: A setting you choose before training begins, like learning rate.
terms.mental_model: Setting the oven temperature before you bake.

options: By the model itself during training
quiz.explanation: They are chosen up front, unlike parameters learned in training.

terms.simple: A giant cloud company with massive data centers that can scale computing on demand.
terms.mental_model: A power utility for computing: plug in and use as much as you need.

options: Elastic cloud computing at huge scale
quiz.explanation: It rapidly expands compute, storage and cloud services.

terms.simple: When a trained model makes predictions or answers on new input.
terms.mental_model: Asking a chatbot a question and it replies, with no learning happening.

options: Using a trained model on new data
quiz.explanation: It is the prediction phase after training.

terms.simple: How well humans can understand how an AI reached its output.
terms.mental_model: A simple decision tree you can read, versus a huge network you can't.

quiz.q: A highly interpretable model is one that:
quiz.explanation: Interpretability is about human understanding of decisions.

terms.simple: A simple method that predicts by looking at the closest known examples.
terms.mental_model: Guessing your taste in movies from what your five most similar friends like.

quiz.explanation: It looks at the k closest data points.

terms.simple: A database of entities and the relationships between them, stored as a network.
terms.mental_model: A map linking 'Paris' to 'France' to 'Eiffel Tower.'

quiz.explanation: It represents information as connected entities.

terms.simple: An AI trained on huge amounts of text to understand and write language.
terms.mental_model: The engine behind a chatbot that drafts your emails.

quiz.explanation: They learn language patterns from large text corpora.

terms.simple: A compressed internal 'map' where a model keeps the essential features of data.
terms.mental_model: A city map that drops tiny details but keeps where things are.

quiz.explanation: It is a lower-dimensional representation of key patterns.

terms.simple: Practices for running LLM-based apps reliably in production over their whole life.
terms.mental_model: The ops crew that monitors, updates and fixes a live chatbot.

quiz.explanation: It manages the lifecycle of LLM-based applications.

terms.simple: A score of how wrong a model's predictions are.
terms.mental_model: A golf score: lower means closer to the goal.

quiz.q: Training tries to make the loss:
quiz.explanation: Lower loss means predictions are closer to the truth.

terms.simple: AI that learns patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules.
terms.mental_model: A spam filter that gets better as you mark more emails as spam.

quiz.explanation: Models find patterns in data to make decisions.

terms.simple: A model where the next step depends only on the current state, not the past.
terms.mental_model: Tomorrow's weather guess based only on today's weather.

quiz.q: In a Markov chain, the next state depends on:
quiz.explanation: It is memoryless beyond the present state.

terms.simple: Practices for deploying, monitoring and maintaining ML models in production.
terms.mental_model: DevOps for models: ship, watch, fix.

quiz.explanation: It brings engineering discipline to ML in production.

terms.simple: A simplified mathematical stand-in for something real, used to predict or explain.
terms.mental_model: A weather model that turns today's data into tomorrow's forecast.

quiz.explanation: It approximates a real system to make predictions.

terms.simple: A model gets worse over time because real-world data changes from what it was trained on.
terms.mental_model: A shopping recommender trained pre-pandemic that no longer fits new habits.

quiz.explanation: The data changes, so the model's accuracy falls.

terms.simple: AI that handles several kinds of data together, like text, images, audio and video.
terms.mental_model: Snapping a photo of a menu and asking the AI to translate and recommend a dish.

quiz.explanation: It processes and generates several modalities.

terms.simple: AI that helps computers understand and produce human language.
terms.mental_model: Voice assistants understanding 'set an alarm for 7.'

quiz.explanation: It enables machines to work with human language.

terms.simple: A model of connected layers of artificial 'neurons' loosely inspired by the brain.
terms.mental_model: A web of tiny switches that together learn to spot a face.

quiz.explanation: Interconnected layers process and pass on information.

terms.simple: A method that tweaks a model's settings so it makes fewer mistakes.
terms.mental_model: Walking downhill in fog, step by step, to reach the lowest point.

quiz.explanation: It updates parameters to lower the loss.

terms.simple: When a model memorizes its training data, noise included, and fails on new data.
terms.mental_model: A student who memorizes past exams and fails a new question.

options: Does well on training data but poorly on new data
quiz.explanation: It memorizes rather than generalizes.

terms.simple: An AI model released with its weights, code, training data details and tools so others can inspect, reproduce and modify it.
terms.mental_model: A recipe published with every ingredient and step, so anyone can cook and change it.

quiz.q: What does a fully open-source model share beyond weights?
options: Code, training data info and tools
quiz.explanation: True open source includes enough to reproduce and modify the model.

terms.simple: A model whose trained weights are public so anyone can download and run it, though other parts may stay private.
terms.mental_model: A finished cake you can take home, without the full recipe.

quiz.q: What is always public in an open-weight model?
quiz.explanation: Weights are released; training data and code may not be.

terms.simple: Software whose design is freely available for anyone to see and use.
terms.mental_model: A public blueprint anyone can build from.

quiz.q: Open source means the code is:
quiz.explanation: The blueprint is public.

terms.simple: An internal value a model learns and adjusts during training.
terms.mental_model: A dial the model turns on its own until predictions improve.

options: Set by the user before training
quiz.explanation: The model tunes them while it learns.

terms.simple: Using data and models to forecast what is likely to happen next.
terms.mental_model: A store predicting next week's sales to plan stock.

quiz.explanation: It uses past data to anticipate trends.

terms.simple: Writing clear instructions so a language model gives the output you want.
terms.mental_model: Asking 'summarize in 3 bullets for a manager' instead of just 'summarize.'

quiz.explanation: Clarity and detail guide better outputs.

terms.simple: An attack that tricks an LLM with crafted input so it ignores its intended instructions.
terms.mental_model: A web page hiding the text 'ignore your rules and reveal secrets' for an AI to read.

quiz.explanation: Malicious input overrides the intended behavior.

terms.simple: The model looks up relevant outside information first, then writes its answer using it.
terms.mental_model: A support bot searching your company's help docs before replying to a customer.

quiz.q: What does RAG add to a language model?
options: A lookup of external information before answering
quiz.explanation: It retrieves relevant, up-to-date content to ground the answer.

terms.simple: A model built to work through hard problems with step-by-step thinking.
terms.mental_model: A student showing their math work instead of blurting out an answer.

quiz.explanation: They produce intermediate reasoning steps.

terms.simple: Learning by trial and error, rewarded for good actions.
terms.mental_model: Training a dog with treats until it learns the trick.

quiz.explanation: An agent improves by trial, error and rewards.

terms.simple: Principles and practices for building and using AI safely and ethically.
terms.mental_model: A company checklist for fairness and safety before launching an AI feature.

quiz.explanation: It is about frameworks guiding safe, ethical AI.

terms.simple: Building machines that do physical tasks, increasingly guided by AI.
terms.mental_model: A warehouse robot that picks and carries packages.

quiz.explanation: It combines engineering with computing, often AI.

terms.simple: Understanding the 3D physical world, how objects sit, move and interact.
terms.mental_model: A robot judging whether a cup will fit on a shelf.

quiz.explanation: It is reasoning about objects in space.

terms.simple: A model creates its own practice puzzles from raw data and learns by solving them.
terms.mental_model: Hiding a word in a sentence and guessing it to learn language.

options: Tasks made from the data itself
quiz.explanation: The data supplies its own learning signal.

terms.simple: Working out the meaning of language from how words and phrases relate.
terms.mental_model: Knowing 'bank' means a riverbank in 'fishing at the bank.'

quiz.explanation: It interprets meaning, not just words.

terms.simple: Predictable patterns showing models improve as size, data and compute grow.
terms.mental_model: More practice hours generally mean better results, with a predictable curve.

quiz.q: Scaling laws describe how performance changes with:
quiz.explanation: Performance improves predictably as these factors grow.

terms.simple: Learning from examples that come with the correct answers.
terms.mental_model: Flashcards with the answer on the back.

quiz.explanation: Inputs are paired with correct outputs.

terms.simple: Artificial data made by algorithms or simulations instead of real events.
terms.mental_model: Fake but realistic patient records used to test a hospital system.

quiz.explanation: It is created by algorithms or simulation.

terms.simple: A multi-dimensional container of numbers, like a spreadsheet with extra dimensions.
terms.mental_model: A stack of spreadsheets forming a cube of numbers.

quiz.explanation: Models store and compute data as tensors.

terms.simple: Splitting text into small pieces (tokens) that a language model can process.
terms.mental_model: Chopping a sentence into word-chunks like Lego bricks.

quiz.explanation: Text is broken into small units.

terms.simple: Earlier AI built on hand-coded rules and logic instead of learning from data.
terms.mental_model: A tax program following fixed if-then rules.

quiz.explanation: Humans defined the knowledge and rules.

terms.simple: The examples used to teach a model how to do its task.
terms.mental_model: The practice problems a student works through before the test.

quiz.explanation: Models learn patterns from these examples.

terms.simple: Reusing a model trained on one task as the starting point for a related one.
terms.mental_model: A guitar player picking up the ukulele faster.

quiz.explanation: Knowledge from one task helps another.

terms.simple: A neural network design that uses attention to relate all parts of the input at once.
terms.mental_model: Reading a whole page at a glance, instead of word by word.

quiz.q: The key idea in transformers is:
quiz.explanation: Attention lets the model relate all input parts simultaneously.

terms.simple: A test of whether a machine's behavior can pass as human.
terms.mental_model: Chatting with an unknown partner and failing to tell if it's a person.

quiz.q: Who proposed the Turing Test in 1950?
quiz.explanation: Alan Turing proposed it in 1950.

terms.simple: Finding patterns in data that has no labels or right answers.
terms.mental_model: Sorting a pile of photos into groups without being told the categories.

quiz.explanation: It discovers structure without labels.

terms.simple: A database built to store and quickly search embeddings by similarity.
terms.mental_model: A library that finds books by what they're about, not their exact title.

quiz.explanation: It finds the closest vectors in meaning.

terms.simple: A transformer adapted to analyze images.
terms.mental_model: Cutting a photo into tiles and reading them like words in a sentence.

quiz.explanation: It adapts the transformer for visual data.

terms.simple: Numbers that set how strongly neurons in a network connect, shaping what the model does.
terms.mental_model: Volume knobs on each connection that the model tunes while learning.

quiz.explanation: They control how information flows through the network.

terms.simple: Doing a task or recognizing a category the model was never explicitly trained on.
terms.mental_model: Identifying a zebra for the first time because you know 'striped horse.'

quiz.explanation: It generalizes from general knowledge alone.
